releaseClaim.userOperation: An operator opens the console, changes the model for the system, an agent, a team member or a live conversation using pickers only, and the next turn in open conversations uses it on every replica; settings persist in the database, survive restart, and YAML changes never prevent startup.
supportedEnvironments: web console against embedded SurrealDB 4.0.0 (default features)
web console against remote SurrealDB with at least two UAR replicas on one store
web console against Postgres (postgres-backend feature) with at least two UAR replicas on one store
releaseClaim.currentCapabilities: Today the console receives realtime invalidations over /api/live on embedded Surreal, remote Surreal and Postgres, but coverage is per topic: conversation policy publishes nothing on any store, provider changes invalidate the settings topic instead of providers on Surreal, no writer feeds the models topic, the default-provider change has no dedicated topic, and team and binding topics are internal. Apart from governance.enabled every change event returns through the database change feed; replicas do not refresh their in-memory registry or settings from it. The live system default can be changed only through POST /api/providers/{id}/default; llm.default_provider takes effect only at boot while the settings API reports the edit as effective. None of the 15 "no reader" settings namespaces is read from the settings database, and keys outside server, security and persistence are reported effective although no code reads them. Catalog Model identity diverges between provider-qualified and bare ids. A running team is blocked by any binding revision change, including a member model change, and route edits surface as TEAM_REVISION_CONFLICT or TEAM_ROUTE_PROFILE_MISMATCH. Hot reload already validates and keeps the current config, but a YAML that fails to load stops the next start, there is no last-known-good on disk, and bad persisted embedding values or a malformed provider row can also stop boot. Postgres support is the optional postgres-backend feature, not in default features.

requiredSafetyChecks.description: Capability inversion: an agent-kernel attempt to mutate settings or the default provider is refused at the host boundary and changes nothing; only the trusted host route changes the default.
Persist before publish for defaults: a failed persist of the system default publishes no topic frame and leaves the live default unchanged on every replica.

Masked-secret round trip: a secret setting reads back masked, saving the masked value unchanged keeps the stored secret, and the secret never appears in API responses, drift, reload or resolve bodies, or logs.

Test scripts never require, mint, renew or send authentication credentials (JWTs, bearer tokens, login credentials, admin keys). Provider API keys for scratch stub providers are fixture data and allowed. Enforced by the independent runner review before any scenario command; the listed scenarios state it in their isolation (CFG rows state only that their sentinels are fabricated, so they are not listed).
Seeding and reconciliation add configuration defaults without overwriting operator values: operator-edited rows keep their values across seed, reload and restart while YAML additions merge.
Security refusals never fall back to last-known-good: a configuration that fails validation stops startup before any listener binds.

Nothing secret from the environment is persisted to disk by the fallback: the last-known-good copy holds only validated source bytes, with restrictive file modes and no environment secret (a secret written inline in the YAML itself is duplicated by design).
